title: Production of Recombinant EnvA Rabies Virus
author: Allen Institute for Brain Science
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bdvvi666
materials: Production of Recombinant EnvA Rabies Virus

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Media
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary growth media and ensure antibiotics are added to bacterial media immediately before use.

substeps.instruction: Prepare DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% Antibiotic-Antimycotic by adding 50 ml of FBS and 5 ml of Antibiotic-Antimycotic to 500 ml of DMEM; store at 4ºC.

steps.title: Construct Transgene Plasmid
steps.instruction: Clone the transgene of interest into the G locus of the Rabies CVS-N2c(ΔG)-EGFP genomic plasmid.

substeps.instruction: PCR amplify transgenes of interest using a high-fidelity polymerase and perform PCR purification.
Digest the PCR amplification products and the CVS N2c (ΔG)-EGFP plasmid with appropriate restriction enzymes (compatible with XmaI, KasI, or NheI).
Perform electrophoresis of digested products in 1% agarose gel/SYBR in 1X TAE buffer.
Extract bands of interest under blue light, followed by gel purification and elution into water.
Ligate digested PCR products to the rabies viral backbone using a rapid ligation kit.
Transform chemically competent Stb3 cells with the ligation mix and plate on agarose plates containing Carbenicillin.

steps.title: Screen and Amplify Plasmid
steps.instruction: Identify and scale up the production of the correct recombinant plasmid.

substeps.instruction: Incubate plates at 37ºC overnight (up to 24hr due to large plasmid size).
Pick at least 4 colonies per plasmid and start mini cultures in 2 ml LB media containing Carbenicillin (100 μg/ml).
Extract plasmid DNA using a Plasmid Mini Prep Kit after overnight incubation.
Confirm correct plasmids via restriction digest and sequence 2 correct plasmids to confirm inserts.
Perform maxi culture: start with 100 ml LB media containing Carbenicillin in the morning, then add fresh LB media containing Carbenicillin (100 μg/ml) in the evening to reach a total of 500 ml.

steps.title: Recover CVS N2c (ΔG) Virus
steps.instruction: Rescue the virus from cDNA using B7GG cells.

substeps.instruction: Split B7GG cells into 15-cm plates one day before transfection to reach 60-80% confluence on the day of transfection.

Co-transfect B7GG cells using Lipofectamine with the following constructs per 15-cm plate: 30 µg CVS-N2c (ΔG) genomic plasmid, 15 µg pTIT-N, 7.5 µg pTIT-P, 7.5 µg pTIT-L, 5 µg pCAGGS-N2c(G), and 9 µg T7 polymerase.
At 24 hr post-transfection, feed cells with fresh medium and move to an incubator at 35°C and 3% CO2.
Feed cells with fresh medium every 2 days and split 1:2 every 4 days; monitor for fluorescence markers (may take up to 7 days).
Collect supernatants upon first appearance of fluorescent cells and continue until 10 days after maximal infection.
Filter supernatants at 0.45 µm; store at 4°C (weeks) or -80°C (long-term).

steps.title: Concentrate Recovered Virus
steps.instruction: Concentrate the rescued virus via ultracentrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Weight ultracentrifugation tubes to ensure weight difference is < 0.05 g.
Load 38 ml of supernatant into ultracentrifugation tube 326823, seal with parafilm.
Centrifuge for 2 hours at 700,000 rcf using a SW 32 Ti rotor.
Resuspend the viral pellet in 30 µl of HBSS.

steps.title: Amplify CVS N2c (ΔG) Virus
steps.instruction: Scale up the virus production in B7GG cells.

substeps.instruction: Split B7GG cells into 15-cm plates one day prior to reach 60-80% confluence; replace with 20 ml fresh medium on the day of infection.
Infect cells by adding viral resuspension (equivalent of 220 ml of filtered supernatant per plate).
At 24 hr post-infection, feed cells with fresh medium and maintain at 35°C and 3% CO2.
Feed cells every 2 days and split 1:2 every 4 days.
Collect supernatants from first appearance of fluorescence up to 10 days after maximal infection; filter at 0.45 µm.

steps.title: Test Virus Yield
steps.instruction: Determine the yield of amplified virus using 293 cells.

substeps.instruction: Take 38 µl of supernatants from different collection batches and concentrate as described in the recovery concentration step (resuspend pellet in 30 µl HBSS).
Seed 293 cells into 24-well plates the day before.
Add 5 µl of viral resuspension to each well and observe fluorescence 24-36 hr later.

steps.title: Pseudotype Virus with EnvA
steps.instruction: Pseudotype the G-deleted rabies virus using BHK-EnvA cells.

substeps.instruction: Split ten 15-cm dishes of BHK-EnvA cells one day prior to reach 60% confluency.
Replace medium and add unpseudotyped G-deleted rabies virus (equivalent of 50 ml filtered supernatant per plate).
Incubate overnight at 37°C in 5% CO2.
Remove medium, rinse cells 3 times with PBS, and digest with TrypLE to remove unpseudotyped viruses.
Split cells into 20 new plates and incubate at 35°C in 3% CO2 overnight.
Remove media the next day and replace with 20 ml fresh medium.
Collect culture supernatant every 2 days; split cells when they reach 90% confluency.
Collect three batches of supernatants, filter through 0.45 μm, and store at 4°C.

steps.title: Final Virus Concentration
steps.instruction: Perform a second round of ultracentrifugation for high-titer pseudotyped virus.

substeps.instruction: Load pseudotyped virus into ultracentrifugation tubes 344624 and seal with parafilm.
Centrifuge for 2 hours at 70,000 g using the SW 60 Ti rotor.
Re-dissolve pellets in 100-500 µl of HBSS.

steps.title: Measure Biological Titer
steps.instruction: Titer the EnvA CVS-N2c (ΔG) virus using HEK293-TVA cells.

substeps.instruction: Digest a full 15-cm plate of HEK293-TVA cells with TrypLE and resuspend in 10 ml fresh medium.
Dilute 2 ml of cell suspension with 10 ml fresh medium and seed 500 μl into each well of a 24-well plate.
Prepare a tenfold serial dilution of the viral preparation (10⁻³ to 10⁻⁸).
Add 250 μl of each viral dilution (A–F) to the cells (final volume 750 µl) in triplicate.
Incubate at 35°C in 3% CO2; observe fluorescence 24–36 h post-infection.
Three days post-infection, count infected cells and calculate biological titer (infectious units/ml).
